slides.title: Time and Daily Life
bullets: Prepare to read, discuss and write
slides.narration: Welcome to Grade 3 English, Unit 3: Time and Daily Life. In this unit you will learn all about time and daily life. You will name the twelve months of the year and put them in order. You will talk about your daily routine — what you do at each hour of the day. You will learn to talk about the past (what already happened), the present (what happens every day), and the future (what will happen soon). By the end, you will be able to make your own calendar, just like Amal does in this unit’s story, “The Calendar on the Wall”. In this short lecture, preview the key ideas and prepare for the independent lesson.

slides.title: What you will achieve
bullets: Name and spell the twelve months of the year, in order.
Talk about your daily routine using the hours of the day.
Use the Present Simple to talk about what you do every day.
slides.narration: By the end of this unit, you will be able to name and spell the twelve months of the year, in order. You will also talk about your daily routine using the hours of the day. You will also use the Present Simple to talk about what you do every day. Keep these goals in mind as you work.

slides.title: Words to learn
slides.narration: Your vocabulary work begins with these words: January, February, March, April, May, June. Listen to each word, look at what it means, and try to use it when you talk and write.

slides.title: Read and think
bullets: Point to the words that show it
slides.narration: The reading sequence includes My Day, Hour by Hour and The Twelve Months. Read slowly, look at the pictures, and find the big idea in each text. When you answer a question, point to the words that show it.

slides.title: Present Simple
bullets: We use the Present Simple to talk about things that happen again and again, and about facts that are always true. It is the “routine tense”. When we say...
Try it in your own sentences
slides.narration: The first language focus is Present Simple. We use the Present Simple to talk about things that happen again and again, and about facts that are always true. It is the “routine tense”. When we say “She marks the calendar every morning,” we mean she does it regularly. This helps us describe our daily life clearly. Look at the examples, then try the pattern in your own sentences.

slides.title: Use English for a real purpose
bullets: Say it, write it, make it better
slides.narration: In speaking, you will complete Speaking 1 — My Daily Routine. Say your ideas clearly and listen to your partner. In writing, you will draw, trace, copy or write, then check your work with a grown-up or the AI tutor.

slides.title: You are ready to begin
bullets: Activities, quiz and optional live sessions
slides.narration: You are ready to begin. Start with the words, then the reading and the questions, then the grammar, speaking and writing. Ask the AI tutor for help any time, and bring your questions to a live session too if you join one.
